Definition: a primary verb; properly, to hinder, i.e. (by implication) to injure:--hurt.
BiblicalUsage: To hurt is the word for hindering, injuring — and it appears twice, both times in a promise of protection. In Luke 4:35 the devil comes out of the man and hurts him not. In Mark 16:18 Jesus says his disciples shall take up serpents, and if they drink any deadly thing, it shall not hurt them.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the two verses belong together: the devil could not hurt the man, and the poison could not hurt the disciple, because the Lord stood between.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
